title: boot-benchmark-v1
description: A SEALED, deterministic record of ONE mesh-actor BOOT, captured as a benchmark. It is the boot-time sibling of manual-procedure-record-v1: instead of a reviewer stepping through TC-00..TC-10 in the viewer, the RECORDER (a host process) starts a session BEFORE the actor boots, captures the boot as an image stream, and correlates milestone markers the guest emits so the record benchmarks the from-source first boot (build lbabus ~8s + form the host-only mesh). A booting console has no viewer monotonic counter, so the anchor is DUAL-CLOCK: the host capture timeline (hostMonotonicMs, the visual/frame-pin clock) plus the guest CLOCK_MONOTONIC (guestMonotonicMs, authoritative for cross-plane timing). On seal, raw pixels are DISCARDED; only the dual-clock anchor + per-frame perceptual fingerprints + integrity hashes + the timing spans remain. Cross-plane rule (why the seal tags each span): GUEST-clock spans (buildMs, meshFormMs) are cross-plane comparable; the HOST-clock span (bootToMeshMs) includes hypervisor firmware (BIOS/GRUB) and is WITHIN-plane only. The visual delta is a WITNESS (tolerance + optional ROI mask over volatile cursor/clock regions), NOT the hard gate; the guest-clock timing spans are the regression gate.

iteration.description: The identity being benchmarked (box tag, the pinned collab-cli source ref the actor built, or a build id). Cross-iteration diff pairs two records with different iteration values.

sessionId.description: Unique id for this boot-capture session.

sealedAt.description: UTC timestamp when the record was correlated + sealed (raw frames discarded).

plane.description: Which plane recorded this boot. LINUX = VirtualBox recorder; WIN = VMware recorder. The recorder CORE + schema are shared; only the capture backend differs (capture.backend).

hypervisor.description: The hypervisor running the booted actor. Governs which host-clock spans are comparable to which other records (host-clock spans include this hypervisor's firmware).

capture.description: HOW the boot image stream was grabbed. Recorded so a sealed record declares its capture path; the schema is capture-backend-agnostic (no Tools/login assumption).

backend.description: The capture backend. vbox-screenshotpng = `VBoxManage controlvm <vm> screenshotpng` (works from power-on, headless). vmware-vnc = a framebuffer grab off the VM's built-in VNC console (RemoteDisplay.vnc.enabled) — NOT `vmrun captureScreen`, which is VMware-Tools+login-gated and cannot see the boot window.

transport.description: The concrete capture command/mechanism, e.g. 'VBoxManage controlvm screenshotpng' or 'vnc://127.0.0.1:5901 framebuffer'.

cadenceHz.description: Nominal capture cadence (frames/second), e.g. 2. The visual frame-pin resolution is ~1/(2*cadenceHz)s; timing accuracy is guest-clock and does NOT depend on this.

procedure.description: The boot 'procedure' this session recorded: the ordered milestones expected during a from-source first boot.

milestones.description: The ordered boot milestones (caseIds). Canonical: BOOT-START, LBABUS-BUILD-START, LBABUS-BUILT, MESH-OK. Every declared milestone MUST be pinned to a frame for the record to seal.

fingerprintAlgo.description: The perceptual-fingerprint algorithm, RECORD-level. Pinned to dhash-64 (integer-only -> bit-identical cross-plane) via the shared fingerprint.mjs. The cross-iteration diff asserts both records match before comparing.

fingerprintSpecVersion.description: The pinned preprocessing-spec version of the shared fingerprint.mjs (FINGERPRINT_SPEC_VERSION). Two records must share it to be comparable.

anchor.description: The DUAL-CLOCK time anchor + the milestone correlation that CLOSED the record. hostT0MonotonicMs is the pre-boot host reference (t0). The record seals only when EVERY declared milestone is pinned to a frame AND the serial-emitted guest monotonic cross-checks the authoritative journald guest monotonic within skewToleranceMs (a bad/misaligned pin fails closed).

source.description: The visual timeline is the recorder's host CLOCK_MONOTONIC (a booting console has no viewer counter to read). Milestone timing is anchored on the GUEST CLOCK_MONOTONIC (authoritative, cross-plane), not this host clock.

hostT0MonotonicMs.description: Host CLOCK_MONOTONIC (ms) captured at session open, BEFORE the actor booted. bootToMeshMs is measured from here.

hostClock.description: The host visual-timeline clock: process/host CLOCK_MONOTONIC in ms (frame.hostMonotonicMs).

guestClock.description: The authoritative guest timing clock: journalctl -o short-monotonic (guest CLOCK_MONOTONIC since boot) for the milestone unit log lines. Serial mono= is only the live frame-pin cross-check, never the number of record.

method.description: Serial LBABENCH markers pin milestone->frame LIVE (host-arrival closest frame); journald short-monotonic supplies the authoritative guest ms. skewMs = |serialMono - journalMono| cross-checks the pin.

allMilestonesPinned.description: Every declared procedure.milestone was pinned to a frame. Sealing requires this true.

skewToleranceMs.description: Max allowed |serialMono - journalMono| per milestone; a pin exceeding it fails the seal (suspect pin/clock).

pins.description: One entry per milestone: the frame it pinned + both guest clocks + the skew cross-check.

frameIndex.description: Index into frames[] of the pinned (settled) frame — the frame on screen when the milestone fired.

hostMonotonicMs.description: Host CLOCK_MONOTONIC ms of the pinned frame (visual timeline).

guestMonotonicMs.description: AUTHORITATIVE guest CLOCK_MONOTONIC ms (from journald short-monotonic). Spans are computed from this.

serialMonotonicMs.description: Guest monotonic ms from the serial marker's mono= field (/proc/uptime at emit). Cross-check only.

skewMs.description: |serialMonotonicMs - guestMonotonicMs|; must be <= skewToleranceMs to seal.

frames.description: The BOOT IMAGE STREAM, one entry per captured frame in host-capture order (the 'images once the actor begins to boot'). RAW pixels are DISCARDED on seal — only hostMonotonicMs, a perceptual fingerprint (for cross-iteration visual-delta), and a crypto integrity hash remain. A frame that pinned a milestone additionally carries caseId + guestMonotonicMs + settled:true (the diff/pairing anchor).

hostMonotonicMs.description: Host CLOCK_MONOTONIC ms when this frame was captured (visual timeline anchor).

caseId.description: Present iff this frame pinned a milestone. The cross-iteration frame-diff PAIRS by caseId on settled frames (identical to manual-procedure-record-v1), so WIN's frame-diff consumes boot records unchanged.

guestMonotonicMs.description: Present iff a milestone pin: authoritative guest CLOCK_MONOTONIC ms (journald). Spans are computed from these.

settled.description: true on a milestone-pinned frame (the state at the milestone). frame-diff pairs settled-vs-settled per caseId.

perceptualFingerprint.description: Record-level fingerprintAlgo (dhash-64) hash of the frame — MAGNITUDE-comparable (Hamming) across iterations. Computed by the seal step before raw is discarded, via the shared fingerprint.mjs.

integrityHash.description: SHA-256 of the raw frame bytes. Proves the discarded frame existed + was unaltered, without retaining pixels.

spans.description: The benchmark measurements: durations between milestones, each tagged by CLOCK SOURCE and comparison SCOPE. GUEST-clock spans are cross-plane comparable; the HOST-clock span is within-plane only (it includes hypervisor firmware). frame-diff MUST refuse to cross-plane-compare a within-plane span.

id.description: buildMs = the ~8s from-source build; meshFormMs = build-done -> host-only mesh formed; bootToMeshMs = operator-visible power-on -> mesh (host clock).

from.description: Start reference: a caseId, or 'hostT0' for the pre-boot host reference.

clock.description: guest = guest CLOCK_MONOTONIC (journald); host = recorder host CLOCK_MONOTONIC.

scope.description: cross-plane = comparable VBox<->VMware (guest clock); within-plane = only same-hypervisor-over-time (host clock; includes firmware).

visual.description: Visual-delta policy: a WITNESS, not the hard gate. A booting console has volatile regions (blinking cursor, on-screen clock, DHCP/hostname text) that make raw dhash-64 deltas spurious run-to-run, so the guest-clock timing spans are the regression gate and the visual delta is corroboration with a per-milestone Hamming tolerance + optional ROI mask. WIN owns tuning tolerances; cut 1 defaults are permissive (gated:false).

gated.description: Whether the visual delta contributes to PASS/FAIL. cut 1 = false (timing is the only gate).

hammingTolerance.description: Max dhash-64 Hamming distance still considered a visual match for this milestone (empirically set from baseline boots).

roiMask.description: Optional rectangle to EXCLUDE from the visual comparison (the volatile cursor/clock region). null = whole frame.

seal.description: Proof the record is CLOSED: raw capture discarded, only anchor + fingerprints + hashes + spans retained.

recordHash.description: SHA-256 over the ordered per-frame tuple (index, hostMonotonicMs, caseId|'', guestMonotonicMs|'', perceptualFingerprint, integrityHash) plus the ordered spans — the tamper-evident id of the sealed record.
